faqs.q: Which flanges does the R-41 ring joint gasket fit?
faqs.a: The R-41 ring joint gasket fits ASME B16.5: NPS 5 Class 300 / 600 and 900; API 6B: 5-1/8″ at 2,000 and 3,000 psi. It is a oval or octagonal (Style R) ring supplied new in soft iron, low carbon steel, stainless steel or corrosion-resistant alloy.

faqs.q: What does the number in R-41 mean on a ring joint gasket?
faqs.a: R-41 is a Style R ring and the number identifies one ring size and groove. The R-41 has a pitch diameter of 7.125 in (180.98 mm). The same number in a different style is a different ring, so always quote the style as well as the number.

faqs.q: What are the dimensions of the R-41 ring joint gasket?
faqs.a: For the R-41: pitch diameter 7.125 in; width 0.438 in; height, oval 0.690 in; height, octagonal 0.630 in; width of flat, octagonal 0.305 in; radius, octagonal 0.060 in. These are the nominal ring dimensions in inches with millimetres in the size table; confirm the tolerance against your flange groove before ordering.

faqs.q: Should I order the R-41 oval or octagonal?
faqs.a: Order the R-41 octagonal for flat-bottom grooves, which are standard on current flanges, and oval only if the groove is round-bottomed, as on some older flanges. An oval ring also seals in a flat-bottom groove.

faqs.q: What pressure can the R-41 ring joint gasket be used at?
faqs.a: ASME B16.5: NPS 5 Class 300 / 600 and 900; API 6B: 5-1/8″ at 2,000 and 3,000 psi. The ring takes the rating of the flange it seals, so check the flange class and the groove, not the ring alone. Use the flange rating as the limit for the R-41.

faqs.q: Which material should I choose for the R-41 ring joint gasket?
faqs.a: Match the flange and the service: soft iron (D, 90 HB maximum) and low carbon steel (S, 120 HB) suit carbon-steel flanges in general service, while 316 or 304 stainless (S316 or S304, 160 HB) and Alloy 625 (180 HB) suit corrosive and sour service. The R-41 must always be softer than the flange groove.

faqs.q: Which standards does the R-41 ring joint gasket meet?

faqs.q: Which other ring numbers sit next to the R-41 in the same style?
faqs.a: In Style R the nearest listed ring is the [R-39 ring joint gasket](/p/r-39-ring-joint-gasket), which seals a different flange size. Ring numbers are not interchangeable between sizes, so confirm the flange before ordering. See the [ring joint gasket guide](/blog/ring-joint-gaskets-r-rx-bx) for the full table.

faqs.q: Can a R-41 ring joint gasket be reused?
faqs.a: No. The R-41 deforms into the groove when the flange is made up, so fit a new ring each time the joint is broken. Clean the groove, check it for damage and do not mix ring styles.

faqs.q: Which material should I choose for the RX-74 ring joint gasket?
faqs.a: Match the flange and the service: soft iron (D, 90 HB maximum) and low carbon steel (S, 120 HB) suit carbon-steel flanges in general service, while 316 or 304 stainless (S316 or S304, 160 HB) and Alloy 625 (180 HB) suit corrosive and sour service. The RX-74 must always be softer than the flange groove.

faqs.q: Which standards does the RX-74 ring joint gasket meet?
faqs.a: The RX-74 is listed to API 6A and is supplied by API-licensed manufacturers with the API certificate and monogram documentation where ordered to API 6A. Each ring is stamped with its number and material code, so it can be matched to the flange.

faqs.q: Which other ring numbers sit next to the RX-74 in the same style?
faqs.a: In Style RX the nearest listed ring is the [RX-73 ring joint gasket](/p/rx-73-ring-joint-gasket), which seals a different flange size. Ring numbers are not interchangeable between sizes, so confirm the flange before ordering. See the [ring joint gasket guide](/blog/ring-joint-gaskets-r-rx-bx) for the full table.

faqs.q: Can a RX-74 ring joint gasket be reused?
faqs.a: No. The RX-74 deforms into the groove when the flange is made up, so fit a new ring each time the joint is broken. Clean the groove, check it for damage and do not mix ring styles.

faqs.q: How do I choose between R, RX and BX rings when ordering the RX-74?
faqs.a: Style R is oval or octagonal, RX is pressure-energised for API 6B flanges, and BX is for API 6BX flanges and does not interchange with the others. The RX-74 is a Style RX ring. Read the [ring joint gasket guide](/blog/ring-joint-gaskets-r-rx-bx) and the [API flange range](/c/flow-iron-flanges-api).
